SMTO-SKL-0056 — A Google Drive file didn't arrive intact

GUID: fac970fc-b060-5f61-82cb-ca7527ec2fec
Slug: google-drive-transfer-integrity-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO checks every file it moves to or from Google Drive. This file came through different from what was expected, so SMTO threw it away instead of saving or uploading a damaged copy.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For a download, check in Google Drive that nobody is editing or replacing the file right now, then ask SMTO to download it again. A file that changes while it's being copied won't match what Google said it would be.
  2. For an upload, add the file to the conversation again with Add files to conversation, then ask SMTO to upload that new copy. SMTO's stored copy no longer matched the original, so a fresh copy gives it something it can verify.
  3. Before asking again for an upload, open Google Drive and check whether the file is already there. SMTO stops before sending a damaged copy, but checking avoids ending up with two copies if an earlier try worked.

What success looks like

  • The downloaded file appears under Artifacts in the conversation, or the uploaded file appears in Google Drive with the right size.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps failing for the same file, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; repeated mismatches can mean a storage problem on the computer running SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Drive transfer failed verification: downloaded bytes did not match the expected size or MD5 checksum, or an upload source no longer matched its registered size and SHA-256.

What this means

  • Downloaded bytes fail expected size or MD5 checks, or upload-source bytes no longer match the registered size and SHA-256. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Downloaded bytes fail expected size or MD5 checks, or upload-source bytes no longer match the registered size and SHA-256.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish download verification from pre-upload source verification and compare exact revision/checksum.

How to fix it

  • For downloads, files.save rejected the stream because the byte count or md5Checksum differed from the file metadata (often the file changed during the download or the connection truncated it); read the file's info again and repeat the download. For uploads, files.source found the artifact's bytes differ from its registered size_bytes/sha256, so nothing was sent; re-register the source artifact and check the artifact store's storage before uploading again.
  • Read the exact file state again and retry the read. Inspect uncertain uploads before repeating them.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the exact file state again and retry the read. Inspect uncertain uploads before repeating them.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended bytes match retained metadata before they are published or sent.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
